---
title: "Research"
---

How does the developing visual cortex arrive at reliable representations of the
outside world? Before eye opening, cortical networks already show structured
spontaneous activity. After eye opening, visual experience reshapes this
endogenous activity into representations that respond consistently to the same
stimulus. My research asks which circuit mechanisms carry this transition.

## Emergence of reliable cortical representations

At eye opening, responses of ferret visual cortex to the same stimulus vary
strongly from trial to trial. Over the following days they become reliable.
Combining chronic two-photon imaging with recurrent network models, we found
that this reliability arises when visual input becomes aligned with the
endogenous network structure, rather than from a general reduction of noise.
See *Trägenap et al., Nature Neuroscience 2025*.

## Feedforward input and recurrent circuits

How do feedforward inputs interact with recurrent cortical circuits during
development? Together with the Fitzpatrick lab we showed that coherent cortical
responses develop as feedforward inputs become more discriminable and better
aligned with the recurrent network.
See *Lempel, Trägenap et al., Neuron 2025*.

## Millimetre-scale selective amplification

With the Smith lab we study how the developing cortex selectively amplifies
particular activity patterns across millimetres of cortical surface, and which
network properties can account for this.
See *Mulholland, Trägenap et al., bioRxiv 2026* (co-first authors).

## Methods

Dynamical recurrent network models, analysis of large-scale calcium imaging
data, and the comparison of model predictions with chronically recorded neural
populations. Research code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/SigridTraegenap).
